nodes.name: Substrate cleaning
nodes.procedure: All substrates were cleaned with acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and water using an ultrasonic bath to remove impurities and dust. In addition, stainless-steel plates and felts were treated with a 10% nitric acid + 0.5% ammonium fluoride solution to generate some surface pickling and remove possible impurities and oxidation layers from their surfaces.
nodes.source_text: All substrates were cleaned with acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and water using an ultrasonic bath... stainless-steel plates and felts were treated with a 10% nitric acid + 0.5% ammonium fluoride solution

nodes.name: NiFe single-layer deposition
nodes.procedure: Metallic NiFe single-layer catalysts were grown (~800 nm equivalent thickness) using an Ar discharge (150 W, 120 kHz, 30 sccm) at a pressure of 5 × 10^{-3} mbar. The deposition rate was ~20 nm·min^{-1}. Before any deposition, a presputtering treatment (50 W, 120 kHz, 5 × 10^{-3} mbar, Ar gas) was applied to clean the target. Substrates were placed on a circular rotatable sample holder (10 cm diameter) located at ~90° with respect to the axis of the magnetron target. The sample holder was axially rotated at a rate of ~5 rpm during the deposition process.
nodes.source_text: Metallic NiFe single-layer catalysts were grown (~800 nm equivalent thickness) using an Ar discharge (150 W, 120 kHz, 30 sccm) at a pressure of 5 × 10^{-3} mbar.

nodes.name: NiFeOx single-layer deposition
nodes.procedure: Oxide NiFeOx single-layer catalysts were grown (~1100 nm equivalent thickness) using the same process conditions as NiFe single-layer but with an even Ar/O₂ ratio (15 sccm each gas) in the plasma discharge. The deposition rate was ~4 nm·min^{-1}. Before any deposition, a presputtering treatment (50 W, 120 kHz, 5 × 10^{-3} mbar, Ar gas) was applied to clean the target. Substrates were placed on a circular rotatable sample holder (10 cm diameter) located at ~90° with respect to the axis of the magnetron target. The sample holder was axially rotated at a rate of ~5 rpm during the deposition process.
nodes.method: Reactive magnetron sputtering oblique angle deposition
nodes.source_text: Oxide NiFeOx single-layer catalysts were grown (~1100 nm equivalent thickness) using the same process conditions as before, but with an even Ar/O₂ ratio (15 sccm each gas) in the plasma discharge.

nodes.name: NiFe/NiFeOx bilayer deposition (gradient)
nodes.procedure: Metal/oxide bilayer catalysts were prepared with a fixed equivalent thickness for the metallic layer (~800 nm) and a varying equivalent thickness of the oxide layer. The interlayer transition between the metal and the oxide layers was made through a metal/oxide gradient layer, keeping fixed the power conditions while increasing by 5 sccm the oxygen flow and decreasing the Ar flow in an equivalent way every 5 min to reach a 15:15 sccm Ar/O₂ flow ratio in the plasma discharge.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe shows fcc Ni peaks at 44.5°(111), 51.8°(200), 76°(220); NiFeOx/NiFe/NiFeOx show fcc NiO peaks at 37.0°(111), 42.9°(200), 62.2°(220), 75°(311) shifted to lower angles (~1% lattice expansion from Fe substitution); crystallite sizes 10-15 nm by Scherrer analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD of the single metal layer or bilayer catalyst (Figure S4 in Supporting Information 4) depicted a series of peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76° that can be assigned to the diffractions of the (111), (200), and (220) planes of the fcc crystal structure of metallic nickel... and at 37.0°, 42.9°, 62.2°, and 75° that can be assigned to the (111), (200), (220), and (311) planes of the fcc structure of NiO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p₃/₂ deconvolution shows NiFe as-prepared: mainly Ni, NiO, Ni(OH)₂ → conditioned: ↑Ni(OH)₂/NiOOH, ↓Ni/NiO; aged: ↑NiO/NiOOH, Fe↑20 at%; NiFeOx/NiFe/NiFeOx-800 more stable surfaces, Fe stable 13-14 at% after aging.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectra deconvolution performed using the B.E. values reported by Biesinger et al. has allowed us to determine the distribution of Ni species at the surface of catalyst samples after the different electrochemical treatments. The results are reported in Figure 4B.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOx/NiFe/NiFeOx-800: Ni²⁺ A₁g(~530 cm⁻¹)/E_g(~480 cm⁻¹), weak Fe-O(~360 cm⁻¹); NiFe as-prepared weak oxides → conditioned/aged: ↑Ni-O band intensity but retains metallic core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the as-prepared state, clear differences are observed... main broad contribution in the NiFeOx and NiFe/NiFeOx-800 samples at ~530 cm⁻¹ (vertical red dashed line) with a shoulder at ~480 cm⁻¹ (vertical blue dashed line). These signals are consistent with the A₁g and E_g Raman active vibrational modes of Ni²⁺ bonds.
